hook.reason: The title line "Throw the gas back, take flight" is concrete, singable and close to the core idea in miniature, and it opens and closes the chorus. It is held back a little because "take flight" is vague. The lesson opens on the learner's own question, "If there's no air in space, what is a rocket pushing on?", and the narration opens on a balloon, which is from the learner's world. The song's i-2 line is a stretched, slightly odd intro.

frame.reason: The skateboarder throwing a heavy ball is an apt picture of the whole job (push mass backward, get pushed forward), and it is used in the song, lesson and narration. In the song it appears in verse 1 and in v2-12 ("the skater's trick"), but it is absent from the chorus, bridge and outro, where the balloon appears instead. The balloon in the intro, outro and narration opening is a second picture that competes with it, though it is the same mechanism.

why_chain.reason: The lesson and narration teach each link in order and give the cause for each: oxidizer so no air is needed, burning makes high-pressure gas, the nozzle speeds it up, the third-law reaction gives thrust, and the "different objects, so they never cancel" point is made explicitly. The lesson's predict section also explains why equal forces give different accelerations. The final link, that it pushes on its own exhaust and so works in space, is made in the misconception section. The song carries the gist, but several tangents (momentum, coasting, thrust at sea level) dilute the chain.

key_lines.reason: Most lines are steps, not labels, for example "Fuel + oxidizer burn → hot, high-pressure exhaust gas" and "Forces act on different objects → they don't cancel". Several problems remain. "No air in space: what does a rocket push against?" is a question rather than a step. Line 4 is pinned to "It hauls a fuel tank and an oxidizer tank", which is the tanks and not the burning. The "Pushes its own exhaust, not air → works in space" line is pinned to "the thrust's a little higher in space". There are ten lines with detours into momentum and coasting, and "Nozzle shoots..." is pinned to a line about speeding the gas up.

errors.claim: Narration n11: "That gas starts in the fuel tank, which holds the fuel."
errors.problem: The exhaust gas does not start in the fuel tank; it is made when fuel and oxidizer burn in the combustion chamber.
errors.correction: Say the rocket carries fuel in a tank, and that the exhaust gas is made when the fuel burns in the combustion chamber.

errors.claim: Lyric v1-9/v1-10: "Its own oxygen, so there's no air it has to thank"
errors.problem: The oxidizer is not always oxygen (it is a supply of oxygen only in some engines); stating it as simply "its own oxygen" is a mild oversimplification, and the line is filler.
errors.correction: Say it carries an oxidizer, often liquid oxygen, so it needs no air to burn.

errors.claim: Lyric v2-5/v2-6 and narration n19: "The rocket's heavy, so it speeds up slow / The gas is light, it gets flung back fast"
errors.problem: Equal forces on the exhaust and the rocket explain unequal accelerations, but the rocket does not simply start heavy and slow; as the song states it, a learner might think the rocket is slow when it is actually accelerating hard.
errors.correction: Say the same-size force gives the light exhaust a huge acceleration and the heavy rocket a smaller one.

accuracy.reason: The core physics is sound: third-law pairs, thrust, the vacuum thrust gain, the first-law coasting and the momentum link are all correct. The one real slip is n11, "That gas starts in the fuel tank", which misplaces where the exhaust is made. Other lines ("its own oxygen", the loose "heavy, so it speeds up slow") are small imprecisions, and the balloon's rubber "squeezes air" is fine. Nothing here is carried away badly wrong.

singability.reason: The chorus "Throw the gas back, take flight / Push the gas left, the rocket goes right" is a clean, singable chant. Verses are rapped and many lines fit that, but some are textbook sentences, such as "Same size, opposite way, an action-reaction pair" and "Conservation of momentum, that's the next chapter's name". Lines like "Its own oxygen, so there's no air it has to thank" and "Than at sea level, where the air pushes back at the engine's base" reach for rhymes or run long. c3-1/c3-2 are an added chorus section that breaks the chant, and the verses are very long.

lesson_clarity.reason: It opens on the learner's question, then gives the big picture, the skateboard picture and the engine steps, with a labelled Predict question answered straight after (equal forces, so why is the gas faster?) and a section for the misconception. The ending check, "what does it push against, and why does that make it move forward?", is good but can be answered by repeating the core idea. The lesson also carries many new terms (oxidizer, combustion chamber, nozzle, thrust, second law, first law, momentum) and sections for coasting and momentum that go beyond what was asked.
